description:
Did We Just Find Signs of Life on Mars?

Episode 89 of a daily journey through the universe. 🧪
Perseverance and the 'Cheyava Falls' rock: in July 2024 the rover found a reddish rock with 'leopard spots' in an ancient river valley in Jezero Crater. In September 2025 a study in Nature called its sample, 'Sapphire Canyon', a potential biosignature. What that means, and what it doesn't.

segments.text: Did a rover just find signs of life on Mars? Look at these spots.
Perseverance landed in Jezero crater on Mars in February twenty twenty-one. Billions of years ago, this crater was a lake.
segments.headline: An ancient lake

segments.text: In July twenty twenty-four, exploring an old river valley, the rover found a reddish rock unlike any other. Scientists named it Cheyava Falls.
segments.headline: Cheyava Falls

segments.text: It was covered in small spots, light in the middle with dark rims. They called them leopard spots.
segments.headline: Leopard spots

segments.text: On Earth, very similar spots can form when microbes feed on chemicals in rocks.
segments.headline: Like microbes on Earth

segments.text: In September twenty twenty-five, scientists published a study saying the sample contains a potential biosignature.
That's the strongest hint yet. But potential means maybe. Chemistry without life might make the same spots.
segments.headline: Potential means maybe

segments.text: Perseverance drilled a sample, called Sapphire Canyon, and sealed it in a tube. It's waiting on Mars.
segments.headline: Sealed in a tube

segments.text: To know for sure, scientists want to study it in labs on Earth. How and when to bring it home is still being decided.
segments.headline: Bring it home?

segments.text: Next stop: You Are Stardust. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for the next stop.
